newsitem.title: UK: Riot flares in Belfast sectarian zone.
newsitem.headline: Riot flares in Belfast sectarian zone.

text.p: Rioting broke out between rival Protestants and Catholics in north Belfast on Saturday, Northern Ireland security sources and media said.
Eight Catholic families fled their homes when Protestant "Loyalist" hoodlums broke into their apartment block, the reports said.
Some 200 youths were involved and one was arrested when police, backed up by British troops, separated the factions and drove the Loyalists back into their neighbourhood.
The disturbances were quelled by nightfall, but security forces remained at the scene where the atmosphere was tense.
The trouble flared at Limestone Road where sectarian anger frequently spills over into trouble between Catholics who oppose rule from British rule and Protestants loyal to London.
The British province has been tense in recent months, with Irish Republican Army guerrillas, who draw support in Catholic zones, and pro-British Protestant extremists launching violent attacks.
